sourceEvidence.claim: The empiric rule (ceftriaxone + vancomycin; ampicillin if Listeria; acyclovir if encephalitis) + the viral set (coxsackievirus, HSV-2, HIV, West Nile, VZV; Cryptococcus in HIV)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Give ceftriaxone and vancomycin empirically (add ampicillin if Listeria is suspected; add acyclovir if viral encephalitis is
suspected).
Viral causes of meningitis: enteroviruses (especially coxsackievirus), HSV-2 (HSV-1 = encephalitis), HIV, West Nile virus (also
causes encephalitis), VZV.
In HIV: Cryptococcus spp.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The vaccine notes (GBS down with screening + prophylaxis; H influenzae down with conjugate vaccines — cases in the unimmunized)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Note: Incidence of Group B streptococcal meningitis in neonates has ↓ greatly due to screening and antibiotic prophylaxis in
pregnancy. Incidence of H influenzae meningitis has ↓ greatly due to conjugate H influenzae vaccinations. Today, cases are
usually seen in unimmunized children.

sourceEvidence.claim: Brain abscess block (viridans + S aureus; dental adds oral anaerobes; multiple = bacteremia; single = contiguous with the lobe map; Toxoplasma in AIDS)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Infections causing
brain abscess

Most commonly viridans streptococci and Staphylococcus aureus. If dental infection or extraction
precedes abscess, oral anaerobes commonly involved.
Multiple abscesses are usually from bacteremia; single lesions from contiguous sites: otitis media
and mastoiditis →  temporal lobe and cerebellum; sinusitis or dental infection →  frontal lobe.
Toxoplasma reactivation in AIDS.

sourceEvidence.claim: The workup text (ESR/CRP sensitive not specific; radiographs insensitive early, useful chronic A; MRI best acute; biopsy identifies)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Elevated ESR and CRP sensitive but not specific.
Radiographs are insensitive early but can be useful in chronic osteomyelitis ( A , left). MRI is best
for detecting acute infection and detailing anatomic involvement ( A , right). Biopsy or aspiration
with culture necessary to identify organism.

kypExtensions.summary: The diarrhea bloody/watery mechanism split; the age-ladder U-shape (the birth organisms returning at life's end) shared by pneumonia and meningitis with the Listeria ampicillin rule; the CSF glucose tiebreaker for the lymphocyte rows; the abscess count-routing with its lobe map; and the osteomyelitis risk-factor swaps — labeled as integrations.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the five matrices without the shared-ladder or routing synthesis; these are KYP's design.
